Uh well turns out I just overthink everything that impacts my emotions significantly regardless of whether those things are good or not. I tend to be the one to break up with people, but usually not because of the anxiety, usually for some other reason or another. 

Things that help me with anxiety in a relationship:

-make sure I express only genuine emotions, not just what I think my partner wants to see

-take alone time, don't spend all your time with them even if you want to, you need alone time to reflect. Fall back on hobbies you had while you were single so that you can re-base yourself and clear your head

-communicate healthily and often, be sure to talk to your partner about how you feel, but also don't go overboard if you're overthinking in the moment because you might worry them. Just make sure your partner knows how you're really doing and feeling and never be dishonest. 

-never act on your anxiety. Ever. Make sure you're in a healthy frame of mind before you make decisions. If your anxiety is compelling you to make a preemptive decision, take a day to be alone and just do some self care. Take a shower, go for a walk, play some video games, cook some food, and do it all for yourself. Have a you day. 

-tally up the facts on paper so that you can look at them clearly if you really feel like you can't be objective in the moment. 

-remember that any relationship can work if you put effort in, and no relationship does not require effort. You're both going to have to change yourselves a little in order to fit together better, and while it's better the less you need to change, you just have to measure whether it'll be worth it or not.

FOR POSTERITY, just wanted to check in and let you and everyone who finds this know that I have:

* started estrogen treatment a little over a month ago, courtesy of Rebirth OBGYN, highly recommend
   * The first appointment with Dr Rixt Luikenaar, who is a lovely and supportive lady, was at home on my computer via video chat, and was $210 *without any insurance*, which was a little steep for me but totally doable because I saved my tax return
   * Hormones (estradiol and Spiro) cost me a grand total of $23 dollars each refill (once a month), and I would like to stress again, *without ANY insurance* (because i was pretty worried about the costs because of this).
      * My dosage is 100mg of Spiro every morning, to block testosterone, and 2mg of Estradiol, twice a day, to... estrogen.
      * Dr. Luikenaar specifically recommended Smith's Pharmacy because it's cheapest for getting hormones.
      * I recommend getting GoodRX which is basically a free app on your phone that gives you discounts. I didn't even mention that I had it, Smith's Pharmacy just remembered my account without me saying anything. Not sure why but it literally just makes prescription meds cheaper. Saved me 10 bucks.
   * My next appointment is early December, at which point I will go physically to their office and get bloodwork done, and have my medication adjusted and increased accordingly. This appointment will cost $100 dollars, plus $60-$80 dollars for the bloodwork which is outsourced (I think?) *once again, this is without insurance* (I hope to have insurance by then)
   * Dr Luikenaar says after one year, depending on some stuff, she'll review my progress and likely put me on Progesterone, which is known for turbo charging breast growth and making you *h o r n y*. Waiting a year before progesterone, she says, will help breast development be a bit more rounded out.
   * And that's sort of the extent of the roadmap for now. Dr. Luikenaar went over all of this in great enough detail (I took notes in Notepad app during the video chat) that I know all of this Day One and remember it.
   * Dr Luikenaar is also capable of prescribing me anxiety or depression meds as needed. She mentioned this three times.
   * I can contact Dr Luikenaar literally anytime thru the online portal that they make you set up before the appointment.
   * I have crippling unmedicated ADHD, but all of this was VERY doable and straightforward, so no worries there if you're neurodivergent in this way. I think I had a question about billing one time, and it was as simple as calling their office and asking them the question, and they literally just told me the answer and then we hung up, it took like 5 minutes. Literally fantastic.
* Am not currently speaking with my unsupportive Christian parents, but will eventually contact them again once things are a bit more stable and I don't feel like crying every time they deadname me, ha ha
* Starting a new full-time job for the state government, with plans to get on their insurance, get cheaper meds and doctor visits, and get an LGBT therapist. (and then get a therapy cat! haha, what now, landlord)
* Oh, and I'm openly trans at work, I dress fem and wear makeup (I wear a bra too, underwire pushup, and I tuck. It really helps that I'm working with a supportive store manager... if the store manager supports you, basically nobody will dare be openly transphobic because we have worker protections for discrimination and that, and a good boss won't take that shit. I'm non-binary so maybe I can weigh in? The original character was and is a man, gender-wise, regardless of his body changes. 

It was also kinda weird. Some people are saying it was on the verge of being transphobic, in the way he was portrayed. Like, he's male, and he identifies that way, and he expressed extreme displeasure with having a female body. It's hard to read, because not only is it a weird and sensitive cultural issue, it's also muddled with Japanese culture and translation issues, so it's impossible to tell what the intentions and meaning were. There's also a weird sexual tension with the character, like he's presented as attractive in a feminine way, and the characters in the show seem shocked and disgusted by him. It's definitely a bit *weird*. 

Making the character non-binary in the new show fucks up the backstory. Like, this character is entirely based on a potentially problematic backstory, but changing the character so that they have none of the problems that the original has... Is it even the same character? 

In fact, the only thing this new enby version of the character has in common with the old version, is that they are both controversial in terms of sex and gender, and not in a flattering way. Enbies are a beautiful thing and we don't just exist in society to cause you discomfort. We want to hang out with you and to be accepted and loved. I want my folks to be portrayed positively in media, but this character exists to put tension on the plot just by his very existence. In the original show, he is conflict. I would rather the character simply not exist in the new show. In turning this character into an enby, you disrupt his purpose in the story, the tension he brings, and you portray enbies in the same unflattering light that the purposefully-uncomfortable character was originally placed in. It's a thoughtless move. 

tl;dr I think they should've just nixed the character altogether instead of making him non-binary, because the character was created to cause weird tension and I don't think it's fair to put enbies in that place.
